beats.narration_text: Here is a practical reading order — seven guides, each with a time estimate so you can slot them into a week. Claude For Dummies, five minutes: the absolute starting point if you've never opened Claude. Claude basics, nine to ten minutes: what you can actually do with it. Claude Cowork, twenty minutes — the core guide to the multiagent mode for non-coders. Claude Skills, fifteen minutes: how to make any recurring task repeatable. Then three more: how to train Claude on your voice, how to get certified for free, and how to stop sounding like AI.

Why are twenty-one guides outdated? Because Claude itself keeps shipping. A guide written about Cowork in January is wrong by March. The model that was smartest in February — Opus 4.6 — is now behind 4.7, which works differently enough that old prompting advice actively misleads you. Popularity is not currency: even widely shared instructions become harmful when the interface and model behavior change. Treat stale procedural content as obsolete.

One additional guide belongs beside the official seven: the Claude Code newsletter, on vibecoding: describing what you want while Claude Code implements it — a website, hosted, with real functionality, zero coding knowledge required. Vibecoding is describing what you want in plain English and letting Claude write every line of code. Specific UI instructions age quickly, but the concept is the fastest-moving part of the Claude ecosystem right now.

beats.narration_text: The practical next step is simple. Save the guide. Block twenty minutes this week — don't read all seven right now, just the first one. Send it to anyone who still hasn't tried Claude or thinks it's a person's name. That last bit is a recurring joke, but it's also a real distribution strategy: the newsletter grows from shares, not ads. Every guide ends the same way because it works. And the strategy itself is a lesson about building with AI — show the work, make it repeatable, let people forward it.

Here's the honest verdict on This seven-guide syllabus. It's genuinely useful — but only if you treat it as a living document, not a finished canon. Claude ships fast enough that any guide older than a few months needs a mental asterisk. The ones on the list that age best are the conceptual ones: how Cowork works, what Skills are for, why you sound like AI. The ones that age fastest are anything touching the UI or model selectors, because those interfaces keep changing. Use the list to orient — then update as you go.
